[[File:Rollie Tesh Spielbound.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Rollie Tesh at Spielbound, Omaha, 2018.]]
'''Roland "Rollie" Leslie Tesh Jr.''' (31 July 1958 – 6 January 2019) co-designed Decipher's ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (SWCCG) with [[Tom Braunlich]]. Braunlich credits him with the ideas that made the game's math work, including [[Destiny]] numbers.<ref name="bp-destiny">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=600s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 10:00–11:03. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221006131758/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref><ref name="wp-swccg">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192945/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="fm-2019">[https://www.forevermissed.com/rollietesh/ Roland (Rollie) Leslie Tesh Jr.], ForeverMissed. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20191014184934/https://www.forevermissed.com/rollietesh/ Internet Archive] (14 October 2019).</ref> He died in Omaha, Nebraska.<ref name="spiel-tweet">[https://x.com/Spielbound/status/1083073953072140289 Spielbound], X (9 January 2019). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015194755/https://api.fxtwitter.com/Spielbound/status/1083073953072140289 Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="fm-2019" />

The credits page of the [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]] rules booklet (1995) thanks Rollie Tesh "for creating an amazing structure, one solitary rule at a time".<ref name="2p-credits">[https://www.hasbro.com/common/instruct/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game.PDF Introductory Two-Player Game Rules Booklet], Decipher / Parker Brothers (1995), credits page. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015192404/https://www.hasbro.com/common/instruct/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game.PDF Internet Archive]</ref>

== Before Decipher ==

Tesh was born in Tampa, Florida.<ref name="fm-2019" /> He met Braunlich through chess at Booker T. Washington High School in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and Braunlich got him into ''Pente''. Tesh held an expert chess rating. ''Pente'' inventor Gary Gabrel recruited both as playtesters at Oklahoma State University.<ref name="rfd14-bio">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=62s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 1:02–3:08. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref> Both became ''Pente'' world champions — Tesh in 1983 — and Tesh proposed the Keryo-Pente variant.<ref name="wp-pente">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pente Pente], Wikipedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008223533/https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pente Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="wp-decipher" /><ref name="fm-life">[https://www.forevermissed.com/rollietesh/about/1 Roland (Rollie) Leslie Tesh Jr.], ForeverMissed. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20211020044947/https://www.forevermissed.com/rollietesh/about/1 Internet Archive] (20 October 2021).</ref> They met [[Warren Holland]] through Pente Games, pitched him a licensed card game while living near Seattle, and designed the [[Star Trek CCG|''Star Trek'' CCG]] (1994).<ref name="rfd14-trek">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=248s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 4:08–6:44. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref><ref name="st-timeline" /> Living on Bainbridge Island near Wizards of the Coast, they met ''Magic: The Gathering'' designer [[Richard Garfield]].<ref name="bp27">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU&t=546s The Booster Pack #27 — The making of the Star Trek CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (10 August 2022), 9:06–10:30. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221006131804/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zK_94pNOPTU Internet Archive].</ref>

== Designing SWCCG ==

Tesh and Braunlich planned the game at [[Richard Borg]]'s house in Florida.<ref name="bp-start">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=186s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 3:06–4:40. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221006131758/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> They moved to Virginia Beach in 1995 to work beside Decipher.<ref name="pilot" /> At first only they and Holland worked on the game with a few staff, until [[Jerry Darcy]] and [[Bill Martinson]] joined. Tesh described the pair's role as coming up with the concepts, which Darcy and Martinson then worked out in detail.<ref name="rfd14-sw" />

The core system grew from a base each player builds up. The base became the deck, and the deck became the Force a player spends and loses.<ref name="rfd14-force">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=616s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 10:16–12:19. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref> Destiny numbers took the place of dice, so the game needed only cards. Strong cards got low destiny.<ref name="rfd14-destiny">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZsJ-sWiL1Iw&t=767s Broadcast 14 – Radio Free Decipher (16 April 1999): Rollie Tesh, Tom Braunlich (Part 1)], Decipher; posted by Player's Council (aired 16 April 1999), 12:47–13:19. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-ZsJ-sWiL1Iw Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 14 transcript]].</ref><ref name="bp-destiny" /> Former Decipher staffer [[Mark Tuttle]] called SWCCG "Tom and Rollie's … game."<ref name="fantha">[https://www.fanthatracks.com/interviews/guest-interview-mark-tuttle/ Guest Interview: Mark Tuttle], Fantha Tracks (15 March 2018). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195155/https://www.fanthatracks.com/interviews/guest-interview-mark-tuttle/ Internet Archive].</ref>

== Later Decipher work ==

Tesh and Braunlich designed the concept of [[Young Jedi]] (1999) from the ''Episode I'' script. Before the film opened, they built a reconstruction of it from details found online and screened it for the team.<ref name="rfd16" /> They also began a ''Harry Potter'' card game for Decipher, which ended when Decipher did not get the license.<ref name="bp-potter">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc&t=3061s The Booster Pack #28 — The making of the Star Wars CCG with Tom Braunlich], The Booster Pack Network (24 August 2022), 51:01–53:07. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20221006131758/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AXdIdJwnjgc Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[The Booster Pack/Episode 28 transcript]].</ref> Tesh is thanked in the credits of the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] rulebook (2001).<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive].</ref>

== After Decipher ==

Tesh published a couple of dozen tabletop games after Decipher, most notably the ''Star Trek'' and ''Star Wars'' CCGs, and Spielbound was the third board-game cafe he worked with.<ref name="spiel-fb" />
